previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for persistent nausea, vomiting, and worsening gastroparesis in the setting of type 1 diabetes and end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis. She developed hypotension and hypoglycemia with altered mental status, prompting a brief MICU stay for observation. Workup revealed no infection, with negative blood and peritoneal fluid cultures, a negative C. difficile test, and imaging showing no acute abnormalities. Her symptoms were attributed to gastroparesis exacerbated by dehydration and diarrhea. She improved with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pro-motility agents including a short course of erythromycin. Her insulin regimen was adjusted due to frequent hypoglycemia, and her tizanidine dose was reduced for safety in renal failure. She was discharged home with optimized medications, dietary recommendations, and follow-up plans with GI, endocrinology, and primary care.
